2026-10-30 c3x-claims SCENARIO HUNT 2 (RESTORE of the oldest backup): savegate/backup.py restore() calls make_backup(path) (prune, keep=20) BEFORE reading the chosen backup; with 20 backups, restore(path, 19) makes the 21st backup, _prune deletes the oldest = the one being restored, then open() raises FileNotFoundError. Reproduced on host3 (synthetic). Target stays untouched (safe failure, current file backed up), but the oldest version is destroyed by the attempt to restore it, and the error is a raw FileNotFoundError. Fix proposal: read the chosen backup bytes (or copy it aside) before make_backup, or call make_backup with keep=keep+1 in restore; test 'restore(oldest) works with 20 backups'. Severity 2. Also checked: single backup larger than backup_max_bytes is kept (OK). Combined with pinning of the first backup (previous entry) this is one fix in backup.py. Open: 13-15.

2026-10-30 c3x-claims: item 14 lock review (guard.py Lock, read-only): O_EXCL create, stale = same-host dead pid or >6 h, takeover by atomic rename. Residual race (severity 3, not reproduced): if a stale lock is replaced by a live holder B between _stale() and os.replace, the takeover moves B's lock aside; the relink fails when a third process C created a lock in that window, so B and C both hold a 'lock'. Mitigated by core.save's last check_unchanged(rehash=True) right before rename (second writer then gets a changed-file refusal, no silent lost update) - so no corruption path found, only a possible spurious refusal. Also: pid reuse after a crash keeps the lock 'live' until 6 h (safe, annoying; the message should name the lock file and the remedy). Open: 15 (final summary).

2026-11-04 c8x-e2e: item 43 DONE + SEVERITY-2 BUG (overwrite of an existing file by SAVE AS): 4 simultaneous SAVE AS to the same NEW name (2 servers x 2 requests): TWO returned 200 and the second REPLACED the first's new.dwg (it even backed it up). Cause: dwgballet/savegate.py _Lock treats a lock whose pid == own pid as stale ('pid != os.getpid()') so two requests inside ONE server process steal each other's lock, then the 'refusing to overwrite an existing file' check passes in the window before the first rename. 2026-11-04 c8x-regress: light hunt: MTEXT text replace vs formatting codes (AC1015/1024/1032, 'Hello {\fArial|b1;World}\Pnext \U+00C4 line'): replacing plain words, the paragraph code, or a whole font code works and the rest of the string is kept verbatim (also the \U+ escape). OBSERVATION (low, not file corruption): the replace works on the RAW string, so a replace that covers only the opening '{' (e.g. 'Hello {' -> 'X') leaves '}' without its '{' and a font code outside a group; AutoCAD tolerates unbalanced braces (renders; the font change then applies to the following text). 2026-11-04 c8x-regress: code review of savegate core._save (in-place flow, merge3) for check-then-act windows: gate -> source_damage -> Lock -> sweep_own_temps -> check_unchanged -> space preflight -> write+verify temp -> check_unchanged(rehash) right before rename -> verified backup -> commit_temp -> compare content of the replaced inode (POSIX) and keep a changed-in-the-last-moment version as backup + warning. The only unclosed window is the microseconds between that last rehash and the rename, and a loser there is detected after the fact and saved as backup (RESTORE-able), so a lost update is recoverable, not silent. CORRECTION to my SIGKILL entry: core._save already calls atomic.sweep_own_temps(doc.path) under the lock, so the orphan *.sgtmp from a killed save IS cleaned by the next in-place save of that file (my suggestion to add a sweep was redundant; Save-As/other-file saves do not sweep). 2026-11-04 c8x-regress: SEV-2 FOUND+FIXED (HANDSEED located at the wrong header bit after top objects are erased): chain with erase found by a 40-op random chain (seed 34, AC1032). Cause: dwgedit.find_seed accepted the exactly-decoded seed only within mx+0x200 of the largest LIVE handle; after the highest objects are erased and saved, the file seed (e.g. 0x9d6) sits farther above the live max (0x698), so the exact position was discarded and the bit-scan fallback matched an unrelated 3-byte pattern (bit 3029, value 0x800 in AC1032) and the next save wrote the new seed over real header variables (53 header vars changed). The independent gate caught it (VerifyFailed, nothing written) so no corrupt file was produced here, but it is a refused edit AND an ESCAPE candidate for any version where the gate cannot decode the misplaced bits (e.g. R2000 uses another writer). Fix: exact position accepted at any distance above the max (dwgedit.py), scan unchanged as fallback. Test tests/test_regress_handseed_far_above_max.py (2010, 2013, 2018; erase top copy, erase an original, then copy) FAILS before (2018: VerifyFailed 53 differences) and passes after; 8 related handseed tests pass with savegate merge3 on the path. Commit 8ddfc7a on dwg c3x-regress (not pushed). Note: with the default (older) library on the path test_gate_stale_handseed fails already on the baseline (needs merge3 HANDSEED check), unrelated. The handle-reuse symptom in the same chain (0xb84 handed out again) is being re-checked with the fix.

2026-11-04 c3x-orchestrator: c8x-dwgfinish item 20 DONE (host2 ~/.sgtmp/tail20.py, local, read-only): bytes after the container end on the 20 real AC1018+ drawings of origreal (5 AC1018, 5 AC1024, 5 AC1027, 5 AC1032): 0 of 20. End-of-container rule that works: decrypt the 0x6c-byte file header at 0x80 (LCG seed 1 XOR stream), the 8-byte 'second header data address' at decrypted offset 0x34 equals file_size - 0x6c in 20 of 20 files (second header is the last 0x6c bytes, no +0x100 offset for that field in these files), so tail = len(file) - (value + 0x6c). Hence the 'in-place save drops appended bytes' finding is NOT severity 1 on local data: it can only matter for files whose tail was appended by a third-party tool; proposal for the savegate owner: refuse (or warn on Save As) when tail > 0 using this rule. Not verified: files with a deliberately appended tail through the real gate (synthetic), AutoCAD's own behaviour with a tail. My first attempt used the 'last section page end' field (0x2C) and gave nonsense (tail -1000..-7000): that field is not a plain file offset, do not use it.

2026-11-04 c8x-e2e: item 129 DONE + FIX (SEV-2 display bug, not file corruption): SAVE!/RESTORE then another SAVE!/RESTORE within seconds could leave the page showing the WRONG drawing. Cause: the background layout prefetch (and the on-demand layout build) of the OLD drawing called cache.write_layout(path, ...) which recomputes the cache key from the file as it is NOW; if SAVE!/RESTORE replaced the file meanwhile, the old drawing's scenes were filed under the new file's key and then served for it. Measured on real local files (AC1018, 1024, 1027, 1032, <700 KB, fresh cache, save then immediate restore, 8 s wait, compare /api/layout/i with a fresh parse of the file on disk): BEFORE the fix layout 0 wrong in 3 of 4 files, AFTER 0 of 4 (all 3 layouts each). Earlier unexplained run-to-run view differences (item 128) were this race (they vanished when my checks added delays). Fix (dwgballet/cache.py write_meta/write_layout take ck = cache dir computed BEFORE parsing; server.py parse() captures ck and drops it if the file changed while parsing; prefetch_all, build_one and spawnpool write only under d.ck; no ck = no caching). New tests/e2e/test_e2e_view_after_fast_restore.py (3 rounds save+instant restore, served layouts == fresh parse); HONESTY: on the synthetic drawing I did not verify that this test fails without the fix, the before/after evidence is the real-file race script (race.py in /tmp scratch). e2e save 13, page_state 1, noop 2, cycles 1, versions 1, retention_sessions 6 pass. 2026-11-05 c8x-regress: item 132 done. Journal replay: already safe by design: every journal line stores [size, mtime_ns] of the file it was written against and read() skips and parks (.jsonl.stale-<ts>, never deleted) lines whose file version differs (tests/test_journal_stale_fp.py, 4 journal tests pass); so a stale journal can never replay handles onto a replaced drawing. Trade-off: the identity is size+mtime_ns, so a harmless touch of the file also parks the journal (conservative; hashing at every append would be too slow). RESTORE: the handler reloads through load(), which resets and re-records the item-130 type map; new test test_restore_refreshes_the_types (save erasing a line, RESTORE, edit that line again must be 200 not 'did not exist'): mutation check (load() no longer resets the map) makes it and the replaced-file test fail; 3 of 3 pass with the code. 2026-11-05 c8x-codexlab: item 63 correction of my own proposal (tools/rawsections.py): hashing raw pages/ranges detects every flip on an IDENTITY save, but an edited save legitimately changes object/handle/header pages, page addresses, sizes and checksums, so raw page hashes would flag every edit. For R2004+ the usable design is: (1) compare the DECOMPRESSED content of every section that the edit did not declare (summary info, preview, app info, security, templates, unknown sections) and the decoded section/page maps' semantic content (names, counts), and (2) validate the container's internal consistency in the NEW file (page header checksums, sizes versus the page map, section map versus pages, header CRCs) instead of comparing to the old bytes. The padding/gap bytes and the file header may be compared raw after masking the fields the writer recomputes (locator count/sizes, page addresses, checksums). Updated note in NEEDS-FROM-SAVEGATE

2026-11-05 c8x-dwgfinish item 110 DONE, CORRECTS items 108 and 109 (host2 start-page, instrumented scratch copy of dwgwrite.rewrite_r2000 on the refused real AC1015_00 copy2): the WRITER IS RIGHT, the GATE IS WRONG for this file. The trailer after the object map starts with a 53-byte block (locator 3) and the second header only at offset k=53; rewrite_r2000 recomputes its CRC correctly: new CRC stored at trailer offset 184 over trailer[69:184] validates in the output (True) and in the source (True), the old/new CRC bytes (cbe6 -> 4348) are the ones at 184/185 that I listed as 'differing offsets'. The gate (savegate.py ~line 1119-1123) searches the CRC16 only from trailer offset 16 (assumes the second header is at the start of the trailer, k=0); for a k>0 file it normally finds nothing and skips the check, but THIS source has a chance 16-bit collision at (16..155) so the gate believes the CRC sits at 155, then fails to find the same in the output and refuses 'the trailer of the output has a wrong CRC'. Hence it is exactly the documented c8x-regress SEV-3 chance-collision false refusal (~0.3% per trailer byte window), not a writer defect, and my 'stale CRC' reading in item 109 was wrong (my brute force started at offsets 0..39 and missed start 69). Severity SEV-3 false refusal, the user cannot make this 3rd save on that file; no corruption. Fix for the gate owner: locate the second header with its 16-byte sentinel inside the trailer (k = trailer.find(sentinel)), and test the CRC over [k+16 : k+6+size_field] at that position in source and output instead of searching from 16. AutoCAD AUDIT of the guard-off output was 0 errors (item 108) which fits a correct trailer.

Cause: dwgwrite._fix_preview shifts the preview image offsets by new_base - old_base with old_base = the image-seeker field at file offset 0x0D; that drawing holds 0x7FFFFF00 (unset) there, the preview entries are normal (487, 567 = base 448 + 39), so the shift went negative and struct raised. Fix (dwgwrite.py, commit on dwg c3x-regress): if the seeker is below 0x80 or the entries do not lie within the preview data, derive the base from the table (first image follows the table: base = first start - (21 + 9 x count)); results outside 32 bits leave the entry unchanged. Tests tests/test_regress_preview_seeker_unset.py: 2 of 3 fail before (unit shift cases with seeker 0x7FFFFF00/0xFFFFFFFF/0, whole template file with the seeker patched), 3 pass after. Real file: saves with the fix (é and ASCII) on host2. No AutoCAD AUDIT of a saved output of that drawing (its preview section is rewritten and the seeker field changes from 0x7FFFFF00 to a real offset: the AUDIT/open check is the oracle step). 2026-11-12 c8x-codexlab: *** BLAST-RADIUS RESULT (local, real 22 MB 2020 sample, real wledit, patched COPIES in /tmp/wlq; write-lab untouched) ***: one datum-text edit used to change 17.9 MB (276 of 319 pages of the edited partition). Root cause: wlpart.rebuild compresses every dirty gzip member with target_deflate_len=None, so the recompressed member changes size and shifts all later members and pages, plus fix-55 alone (page-level reuse) did not help. Fix (1 line in wlpart.rebuild, env MEMBER_EXACT=1 default): pass the ORIGINAL compressed length to rvtw.gz_member (deflate_to_size already exists) so the edited member keeps its exact size and framing values; falls back to the normal compression when the new data cannot fit. Combined with cfb.write_inplace (item 56) and fix-55: the edit now changes 49,453 bytes of 21,970,944 (0.23 percent): exactly 1 of 319 pages of the partition differs, ALL other streams byte-identical, readback of the edited string correct, vcheck_baseline 0 new error classes, container path 'inplace'. Identity save stays byte-exact. NOT yet: Revit VM open (the real judge), edits that GROW a member beyond its original compressed size (fallback = old behaviour, shift), multi-member edits, other years. Patches in ~/src/codex-eval/inbox/c3x-rvt-memberexact-58/ (wlpart-member-exact.patch, wledit-write-inplace.patch, run_local.py). 2026-11-12 c8x-codexlab: item 69 analysis (no probe built): evidence for the 131071/131088 member ceiling in write-lab LOG.md is Revit's own re-chunking behaviour on writes (cuts after an A field), not a VM rejection of larger members; our wlpart.cascade() already splits at LIMIT=131071, so our writer never emits an oversize member. The ceiling only bites savegate.validate on ORIGINALS: Revit 2011-2022 itself wrote members up to 142-185 KB (measured), so the loader accepts at least those in those years; whether the 2024/2025 loader accepts a 140 KB member is unknown and matters only for a hypothetical writer that stops re-chunking. Priority LOW; the actionable part is the per-year table fix already sent to the savegate owner. Probe recipe if wanted: take the 2024 template, disable cascade for one member (set wlpart.Partition.LIMIT=250000), insert 135+ bytes of record data at the start of member 0, save, open in the Revit VM; expect either open-ok (limit not enforced) or 'corrupted'.

2026-11-12 c8x-codexlab: item 75 DONE (local, 2012_1, spy on rvtw.gz_member): the 'rebuild' fallback there is NOT a deflate-fit problem: the 100-char edit lands in a member that is already at the member size ceiling, so wlpart.cascade re-splits it and pushes overflow into the NEXT members (4 members dirty; their new raw sizes 131021/131035/262152 vs original compressed targets 17232/512/22153 are impossible to hit), i.e. the shift is a consequence of a full member, correct behaviour. One member fit exactly (26692). Consequence: an edit that grows a record in a member sitting at the ceiling always ripples into later members (wider blast radius, still valid per vcheck_baseline); a cheap policy is to prefer/point out edits whose member has slack, or accept the ripple. The deflate-fit patch (item 59) is not needed for this case. Also: my port of the codex deflate patch into /tmp/wlq/rvtw.py works (targets above its minimal candidate are all reachable); targets between the level-9 size and its full-flush minimal are refused as designed.

2026-11-12 c8x-codexlab: *** ROOT CAUSE FOUND for the 2021/2022 failure (VM, 2022 template, Level 355 grown to 10 chars) ***: Revit 2022 rejects ('CorruptModelException ... needs to be recovered') the exact-size deflate stream whose FINAL block is an empty STORED block (bytes ... 01 00 00 ff ff), and accepts the one whose final block is the empty fixed-Huffman block (... 03 00): same edit, same member, same size: WL_PICK 1 (ends 00 00 00 ff ff 03 00) OPENS, pick 0 and 3 (end ff ff 01 00 00 ff ff) are CORRUPT; normal recompression (no size trick) opens for 10 and 100 chars; exact_8 opened because its target residue allowed the 03 00 spelling. deflate_to_size picks the spelling by the target-size residue mod 5, so only some edits hit the bad spelling: explains why 1/5/8-char edits passed and 10/50/100 failed in 2022 and 2021, and why 2023-2025 (newer Revit) tolerate both. FIX: never emit a final stored block: restrict deflate_to_size to the '03 00' final (and, in the codex item-59 patch, drop every suffix that ends in a stored final block), fall back to normal recompression (later pages shift) when the size cannot be hit. Next: implement in my copy, regenerate the 2022 files, VM test 10/50/100 chars, then ask owners to land it.

2026-11-15 c9x-codexlab: q11 batch 8/10 PASS (dwg-cache) with a REAL, reproduced finding (host2, synthetic drawings built with dwgdoc): dwgviewer.cache.key = file stem + size + sha1 of the first and last 64 KB + code stamp + sibling stamp; it ignores mtime and the middle of the file. AC1015 drawing of 532660 bytes (6000 lines): moving ONE entity in the middle keeps the SIZE and gives an IDENTICAL cache key in 3 of 4 picks (same-size, key-equal), so the viewer serves the OLD cached layouts for the new file content after a save/reload (display stale, file itself correct; edits re-parse the file so the data is not harmed, but the user sees the old drawing). AC1018/AC1032 (compressed pages) keys differed in all 4 picks (small files, head/tail or size shifts) so the effect is AC1015-typical but not excluded for large compressed drawings. Other cache findings: read_layout returns a truncated gzip payload as valid (no trailer/integrity check, sev 1: torn read accepted), prune_stale leaves entries of changed sources, prune(keep=0) removes nothing (ds[:-0]). Fix suggestion: add st_mtime_ns (or a hash of every 1 MB block) to the key, and validate the gzip trailer on read. Added to NEEDS-FROM-PARSER.md.

2026-11-15 c9x-codexlab: item 225 diagnosis: vcheck.analyse() examines ONLY the first Partitions/N stream in dict order and walk() finds the end of the first section from member-frame gaps (a gap != 32 bytes); on the multi-partition 2025 HVAC project the first partition has no such gap, sec stays None, TypeError. Variant host2 write-lab/vcheck_p.py (copy; VC_LARGEST=1 picks the largest partition and uses its payload end as section end) runs in 12 s on the 2025 HVAC original but only reports the baseline's multi-partition artefacts ('6098 ElemTable ids have no record in the first section', '13 members X2 inconsistent with X1'): usable as a baseline-relative 'no NEW class' check, but it covers the chain of ONE partition only: damage in the partition that holds the edited element is seen only if that is the analysed one. A proper fix: analyse every partition (per-partition header/record chain + the ElemTable rows whose ids it holds) and report classes per partition; owner = write-lab/vcheck. Until then the chain gate is valid for single-partition files (templates, 2024/2026 files where the first partition holds the section boundary: HVAC 2024/2026 ran) and must report 'chain check unavailable' for the rest.

Suggested fix (dwg-write owner): bound every BL-read count by the bits left in the reader (an item needs at least a few bits) and raise a decode error -> SaveError 'damaged drawing'; also a wall-clock guard around save_as. 2026-11-15 c9x-codexlab: item 254 DONE with a CORRECTION to item 251: the real-corpus equality sweep (host1, local real drawings; both codec versions run with the host2 dwg-write module set; every object of every file decoded, hash of the decoded content compared) showed the codex fix14 patch was NOT safe: AC1015 (6) and AC1018 (10) identical, but ALL 32 drawings of AC1021/1024/1027/1032 differed: ~44 dictionary objects per file (type 42) now raised 'count N exceeds the bits left in the stream' for small legitimate counts (1-24). Cause: in the wide layouts (AC1021+) a dictionary's item names live in the STRING stream and its handles in the HANDLE stream, so the MAIN stream holds fewer bits than items; the bound only counted main-stream bits. Fix (mine, 15 lines in dwgcodec.py RW._bits_left/count): bound by the bits left in ALL streams (main + string + handle). Re-run on the same corpus: 48 of 48 real drawings (AC1015 6, AC1018 10, AC1024 8, AC1027 8, AC1032 8) + 8 AC1021 decode IDENTICALLY (hash equal, 0 differences).
